answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label web development is the build stage of a website, carried out by MMC for your agency to present as its own. We take your approved designs and produce working code: templates, back-end features, integrations, testing and documentation, on the platform your client needs.

stages.breaks: Starting a build before the designs are checked.
stages.why: Missing states and unclear behaviour surface halfway through, and the rework is argued over.
stages.does: We review your designs before coding and send you one list of gaps and questions, so the build starts from decisions.

stages.breaks: Editing a live client site to test a change.
stages.why: Clients see half-finished work, and mistakes become incidents with your name on them.
stages.does: Every build goes to a private staging site you can review and forward. Live changes happen only after you approve.

stages.breaks: Hearing about a slipped date on the day.
stages.why: You promised a date to your client on the strength of ours. A late warning leaves you nothing to manage.
stages.does: We flag risk as soon as we see it, so you can reset the expectation with your client in good time.

stages.breaks: Code that only the person who wrote it understands.
stages.why: When that person is unavailable, a simple fix becomes a rescue project.
stages.does: Handover notes, repository access and a short guide for whoever maintains the site next, you or another partner.

stages.breaks: Treating every post-launch request as free.
stages.why: Small asks add up and your margin pays for them.
stages.does: We log change requests against the scope and quote anything outside it, so you can bill your client for it.
